name: Neonatal Severe Cardiopulmonary Failure Due to Mitochondrial Methylation Defect
aliases: Neonatal Cardiopulmonary Collapse from Mitochondrial Methylation Deficiency
Congenital Mitochondrial Methylation Defect with Cardiopulmonary Failure

criteria.description: Onset of severe cardiopulmonary failure within the neonatal period
Laboratory evidence of mitochondrial methylation pathway dysfunction (e.g., elevated homocysteine, abnormal methylation metabolites)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in mitochondrial methylation processes
Cardiopulmonary imaging demonstrating structural or functional abnormalities consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe neonatal cardiopulmonary failure plus biochemical evidence of mitochondrial methylation defect and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to rarity and complexity.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe cardiac failure unresponsive to conventional therapy
searchTerms: newborn heart failure not responding to treatment
refractory heart pump failure in baby

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe neonatal respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
pathognomonic.notes: Progressive respiratory insufficiency in the first days of life

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked lactic acidosis secondary to mitochondrial dysfunction
pathognomonic.notes: Persistently elevated blood lactate levels despite supportive care
searchTerms: high lactic acid due to mitochondrial problems
marked lactic acidosis from energy failure
severe acid buildup from mitochondrial dysfunction
low muscle tone with weak reflexes
floppy baby with poor neonatal reflexes

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive in neonatal period
common.notes: Poor weight gain despite adequate nutrition
searchTerms: failure to grow in early life

common.symptomName: Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
searchTerms: metabolic acidosis with high anion gap
acid-base imbalance with elevated anion gap
blood acidity with increased anion gap

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver detected on physical exam or imaging
Occasional neonatal seizures related to metabolic encephalopathy
Fluid retention due to cardiac failure
Low platelet counts observed in some cases

rare.notes: Limited eye movement due to mitochondrial myopathy
Rare auditory impairment associated with mitochondrial defects
Rare skin manifestations linked to metabolic disturbance
searchTerms: rash related to lactic acid buildup in skin
cutaneous rash linked to lactic acid

laboratory: Elevated blood lactate and pyruvate levels
Increased plasma homocysteine and methylmalonic acid
Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
imaging: Echocardiography showing reduced left ventricular function
Chest X-ray demonstrating pulmonary edema or cardiomegaly
Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in mitochondrial methylation pathways (e.g., MTR, MTRR, or related genes)
other: Muscle biopsy may reveal mitochondrial abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of biochemical evidence of methylation defect
Different genetic mutations unrelated to mitochondrial methylation
Variable onset and response to treatment
Broader metabolic abnormalities without isolated methylation defects
Different enzymatic deficiencies in mitochondrial respiratory chain
May present with multisystem involvement beyond cardiopulmonary failure

redFlags: Rapid onset of refractory cardiopulmonary failure in neonate
Persistent lactic acidosis despite supportive care
Family history of early neonatal death or mitochondrial disorders
